metric: Enterprise GenAI pilot ROI (MIT NANDA project)
value_display: An MIT Media Lab-affiliated project ('The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025') found that roughly 95% of enterprise generative-AI pilots had not yet produced a measurable, rapid P&L impact for the companies running them.
notes: AI-recalled from general public knowledge as of 2026-08, not independently re-verified for this project. A single widely-covered study, not an audited industry census -- methodology and definition of 'pilot' vary by source.

value_display: Gartner publicly predicted that over 40% of agentic-AI projects will be scrapped by 2027, citing rising costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls as the main reasons.
notes: AI-recalled from general public knowledge as of 2026-08, not independently re-verified for this project. This is an analyst forecast, not an observed outcome yet.

metric: Big Tech AI infrastructure capital expenditure
value_display: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta combined have guided to roughly $300-400B in annual capital expenditure for 2025, overwhelmingly attributed to AI data-center and chip infrastructure build-out on earnings calls.
notes: AI-recalled from general public knowledge as of 2026-08, not independently re-verified for this project. Midpoint estimate -- exact figures shift every quarter as guidance is updated; treat as an order-of-magnitude signal, not a precise total.

metric: Share of organizations reporting bottom-line EBIT impact from gen AI (McKinsey)
value_display: McKinsey's annual State of AI survey series has repeatedly found that while most organizations report using generative AI somewhere in the business, only a minority report measurable enterprise-wide EBIT impact from it -- the gap between 'using AI' and 'AI moving the P&L' is the recurring finding, not a single fixed percentage.
notes: AI-recalled from general public knowledge as of 2026-08, not independently re-verified for this project. Deliberately not citing one point-in-time percentage -- the reported figure moves across survey waves; the qualitative finding (a gap exists) is the more durable signal.

metric: Agentic AI market size projections (analyst estimates)
value_display: Analyst market-size projections for 'agentic AI' by roughly 2030 vary enormously by firm and by how narrowly or broadly 'agentic AI' is defined -- estimates in circulation range from the tens of billions to several hundred billion USD, sometimes differing 5-10x for the same target year.
notes: AI-recalled from general public knowledge as of 2026-08, not independently re-verified for this project. Deliberately not picking a single headline number -- treat any single 'agentic AI will be a $X trillion market' claim with skepticism until you've checked its definition and methodology.

metric: Venture funding concentration in AI-agent startups
value_display: AI-agent-focused startups captured a large and growing share of overall venture-capital funding in 2024-2025 according to multiple VC-tracking firms, often at valuations well ahead of meaningful disclosed revenue -- a sign that a substantial share of 'AI money' is flowing into building and staking claims on the technology, not yet into enterprises realizing returns from using it.
notes: AI-recalled from general public knowledge as of 2026-08, not independently re-verified for this project. Directional characterization of a fast-moving funding market, not a precise aggregate figure.

metric: Microsoft 365 Copilot ROI (Forrester TEI study commissioned by Microsoft)
value_display: Forrester's Total Economic Impact study of a composite Microsoft 365 Copilot customer found $36.8M in benefits over three years against $17.1M in costs -- a net present value of $19.7M and 116% ROI -- driven by an average of about 9 hours saved per user per month.
notes: Verified via live web research (2026-09), not AI-recalled. Real published methodology and figures, but Microsoft commissioned and paid for this study and selected the customer inputs Forrester modeled -- treat as a vendor-backed best-case estimate, not an independent audit. Distinct in kind from the named-company case studies in company_case_studies: this is a modeled composite, not one real company's own disclosed result.

metric: GitHub Copilot / Enterprise Cloud ROI (Forrester TEI study commissioned by GitHub)
value_display: Forrester's Total Economic Impact study of a composite GitHub Enterprise Cloud customer found $85.9M in three-year benefits against $18.1M in costs -- a 376% ROI with payback in under six months.
notes: Verified via live web research (2026-09), not AI-recalled. Important caveat: this model bundles the whole GitHub Enterprise Cloud platform (Actions, Advanced Security, tool consolidation) together with Copilot -- it is not a standalone measurement of Copilot's ROI, so attributing the full figure to 'coding agents' alone would overstate it. Vendor-commissioned, like the Microsoft study above.
